I think there are a few key ways in which this would be profitable for industry. Firstly, supply and demand: the higher the worker-to-job ratio is, the more desperate workers will be, and the less money they'll be willing to take. Secondly, relative living standards: third-world workers are used to living in abysmal conditions, so will do without a lot of luxuries we take for granted, consequently have a lower cost of living, consequently be able to accept lower paying jobs. Thirdly, working conditions: a lot of immigrants are willing to work under unsafe or illegal conditions that we wouldn't (including working below the minimum wage). Fourthly, need to support family: a lot of third-world immigrants who live in my country send a considerable amount of their pay home to support their family; as such they are more desperate than those of us with families here, who could get welfare if needed.
Annie Edson Taylor. "Heroine of Niagara Falls." The first person who had ever survived a trip over Niagara Falls in a barrel. At age 63. 1901.

Desiring to secure her later years financially, and avoid the poorhouse, she decided she would be the first person to ride over Niagara Falls in a barrel. Taylor used a custom-made barrel for her trip, constructed of oak and iron and padded with a mattress. Several delays occurred in the launching of the barrel, particularly because no one wanted to be part of a potential suicide.

Two days before Taylor's own attempt, a cat was sent over the Horseshoe Falls to test the barrel strength. The cat survived the plunge and 17 minutes later, after she was found with a bleeding head, posed with Taylor in photographs. Note that the barrellis named: The Queen of the Mist and now the sightseeing boats at the Falls are called The Maid of the Mist.

On October 24, 1901, her 63rd birthday, the barrel was put over the side of a rowboat, and Taylor climbed in. After screwing down the lid, friends used a bicycle tire pump to compress air in the barrel. The hole used for this was plugged with a cork, and Taylor was set adrift near the American shore, south of Goat Island.

The Niagara River currents carried the barrel over the Canadian Horseshoe Falls, which has since been the site for all daredevil stunting at Niagara Falls.

Source.
